From a signal to an interpretation.

  1. Input Signal

    A sensor records a physical change.

  2. Processing Quality

    The system checks whether the signal is usable.

  3. Output Estimate

    An algorithm calculates an indicator.

  4. Context Interpretation

    The result is read alongside operating conditions and limitations.

If quality is insufficient, check placement or repeat the reading according to the manual. Repetition alone does not turn an estimate into a validated measurement.

Conceptual diagram: the actual process depends on the device.

The person is part of the system.

Sleep, attention and the way we interact with an interface help us ask better questions about technology. This space considers both the data and the experience of the person using it.

Understand what lies behind each feature.

Wearables

A device can record signals and turn them into indicators. To interpret them, it helps to distinguish what the sensor detects from what the software calculates.

Artificial intelligence

A useful answer starts with suitable data and a well-framed question. Clarity does not prove correctness.

Advanced technology in a discreet form

The technology of smart rings

Smart rings bring together miniaturised sensors and electronic components that can record different signals related to physical activity and how the body functions.

How the sensors work

Optical sensors

Some rings use photoplethysmography (PPG), a technology that analyses variations in light reflected by tissue to estimate parameters related to pulse.

Motion sensors

Accelerometers record movement and produce estimates related to physical activity and rest.

Temperature sensors

Some devices record changes in skin temperature that can help identify trends over time.

Whether these measurements are available, and how precise they are, depends on the sensors, the algorithms and the conditions of use.

From data to information

Their design allows measurements during everyday activities and rest, combining monitoring technology with comfort and ease of use.

The information collected by the sensors is processed by algorithms that identify patterns and present data the wearer can understand.

A smart device is useful not only because it records data, but because of how it interprets and presents that data.

Algorithms turn the signals captured by the sensors into estimates and indicators that make it easier to follow certain aspects of activity and rest.

These indicators should be understood within the possibilities and the limits of each technology.

Measuring, estimating and interpreting are not the same thing.

Scientific basis

Validating a technology, validating a specific device and holding a health certification are three different things. They are not presented here as equivalent.

Validation of a technology

Publications that study a principle, such as photoplethysmography. That knowledge does not, by itself, establish the accuracy of a product.

Validation of a specific device

Studies that assess the accuracy of a particular model, under the conditions of that test. The result does not extend to other models.

Health certification

Authorisations that apply to a specific medical device. They do not cover other products, or the brand as a whole.

References will be added when a verifiable source exists, with its scope. None are published here yet.

Measuring, estimating and interpreting are different things.

Before accepting a conclusion, we ask what was recorded, how the result was produced and under which conditions it was evaluated. A commercial specification describes a feature; it does not replace a performance evaluation.

  • What data does it use?
  • How was it evaluated?
  • What cannot be concluded?

Our approach to quality

At IGO we look for technological excellence in every category, from the most accessible to the most advanced.

We believe quality does not depend only on price or on the number of features, but on the balance between technology, usefulness and the experience of use.

IGO. Quality is not a product tier. It is our approach.

Understand before you choose.

IGO Research brings together explanations to help you ask better questions when reading a specification: what the device records, what depends on a phone or connection, and what evidence supports each feature. Product capabilities must be checked against the documentation for that model.
